1→# Engram Features
     2→
     3→Engram captures AI agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git. This document catalogs every feature across the CLI, Rust library crates, MCP server, and language SDKs.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Table of Contents
     8→
     9→- [Git-Native Storage Engine](#git-native-storage-engine)
    10→- [Reasoning Data Model](#reasoning-data-model)
    11→- [Session Capture](#session-capture)
    12→- [Session Import](#session-import)
    13→- [Search and Indexing](#search-and-indexing)
    14→- [File Tracing](#file-tracing)
    15→- [Engram Diff](#engram-diff)
    16→- [Context Graph](#context-graph)
    17→- [Branch Review](#branch-review)
    18→- [PR Summary Generation](#pr-summary-generation)
    19→- [Reasoning Blame](#reasoning-blame)
    20→- [Statistics](#statistics)
    21→- [Garbage Collection](#garbage-collection)
    22→- [Remote Sync (Push / Pull / Fetch)](#remote-sync-push--pull--fetch)
    23→- [Git Hooks Integration](#git-hooks-integration)
    24→- [MCP Server](#mcp-server)
    25→- [SDK Integration](#sdk-integration)
    26→  - [Rust SDK](#rust-sdk)
    27→  - [Python SDK](#python-sdk)
    28→  - [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk)
    29→- [CLI Reference](#cli-reference)
    30→- [Architecture and Design](#architecture-and-design)
    31→
    32→---
    33→
    34→## Git-Native Storage Engine
    35→
    36→Engrams are stored as native Git objects -- no sidecar database, no external dependencies, no vendor lock-in. They travel with `clone`, `push`, and `pull`.
    37→
    38→**Object model:** Each engram is a standalone Git commit pointing to a tree of five blobs:
    39→
    40→```
    41→refs/engrams/<ab>/<full-id>  ->  commit ("engram: <id>")
    42→                                    └── tree
    43→                                        ├── manifest.json      Compact metadata
    44→                                        ├── intent.md          Human-readable reasoning
    45→                                        ├── transcript.jsonl   Full session (one message per line)
    46→                                        ├── operations.json    Tool calls, file ops, shell commands
    47→                                        └── lineage.json       Relationships to other engrams
    48→```
    49→
    50→**Key properties:**
    51→
    52→| Property | Detail |
    53→|----------|--------|
    54→| Ref layout | `refs/engrams/<fanout>/<full-id>` with 2-char fanout prefix |
    55→| ID format | UUID v4 hex, 32 characters (no dashes) |
    56→| ID resolution | Exact match, prefix match, or `HEAD` alias (via `.git/engram-head` pointer) |
    57→| HEAD pointer | `.git/engram-head` file updated on every create for O(1) resolution |
    58→| Config | `[engram]` section in `.git/config` (`enabled`, `auto_capture`, `default_agent`, `push_on_push`) |
    59→| Import dedup | SHA-256 `source_hash` on Manifest prevents re-importing the same session file |
    60→| Commits | Orphan commits (no parents) -- engrams form their own DAG via lineage, separate from code history |
    61→
    62→**CRUD operations** (via `GitStorage`):
    63→
    64→- `create(data)` -- serialize and store as Git objects, create ref, update head pointer
    65→- `read(id_or_prefix)` -- resolve ID, load full `EngramData` from Git objects
    66→- `read_manifest(id_or_prefix)` -- fast path, loads only the manifest blob
    67→- `list(opts)` -- enumerate all engram refs, sorted by `created_at` descending, with optional agent filter and limit
    68→- `delete(id_or_prefix)` -- remove the engram ref
    69→- `find_by_source_hash(hash)` -- lookup for import deduplication
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→## Reasoning Data Model
    74→
    75→Every engram captures a complete reasoning unit with five components:
    76→
    77→### Manifest (`manifest.json`)
    78→
    79→Core metadata for fast listing without reading the full engram.
    80→
    81→| Field | Type | Description |
    82→|-------|------|-------------|
    83→| `id` | EngramId | 32-char UUID v4 hex |
    84→| `version` | u32 | Schema version |
    85→| `created_at` | DateTime | Session start timestamp |
    86→| `finished_at` | DateTime? | Session end timestamp |
    87→| `agent` | AgentInfo | Agent name, model, and version |
    88→| `git_commits` | Vec\<String\> | Associated code commit SHAs |
    89→| `token_usage` | TokenUsage | Input/output/cache tokens and cost |
    90→| `summary` | String? | Brief summary of the session |
    91→| `tags` | Vec\<String\> | User-defined tags |
    92→| `capture_mode` | CaptureMode | `wrapper`, `import`, or `sdk` |
    93→| `source_hash` | String? | SHA-256 for import deduplication |
    94→
    95→### Intent (`intent.md`)
    96→
    97→Human-readable reasoning summary, stored as Markdown with structured sections.
    98→
    99→| Field | Description |
   100→|-------|-------------|
   101→| `original_request` | The exact human instruction that started the session |
   102→| `interpreted_goal` | Agent's interpretation of what was being asked |
   103→| `summary` | Brief description of what was accomplished |
   104→| `dead_ends` | Approaches tried and rejected (approach + reason) |
   105→| `decisions` | Architectural decisions made (description + rationale) |
   106→
   107→### Transcript (`transcript.jsonl`)
   108→
   109→Full conversation log, one JSON entry per line.
   110→
   111→| Entry type | Content |
   112→|------------|---------|
   113→| Text | Role (user/assistant/system/tool) + text content |
   114→| ToolUse | Tool name, tool ID, JSON input (Claude format) |
   115→| ToolResult | Tool ID, output text, error flag |
   116→| Thinking | Extended thinking / chain-of-thought text |
   117→
   118→### Operations (`operations.json`)
   119→
   120→Concrete actions taken during the session.
   121→
   122→| Section | Fields |
   123→|---------|--------|
   124→| Tool calls | timestamp, tool_name, input (JSON), output_summary, duration_ms, is_error |
   125→| File changes | path, change_type (created/modified/deleted/renamed), lines added/removed |
   126→| Shell commands | timestamp, command, exit_code, duration_ms |
   127→
   128→### Lineage (`lineage.json`)
   129→
   130→Relationships between engrams and code.
   131→
   132→| Field | Description |
   133→|-------|-------------|
   134→| `parent_engram` | ID of preceding engram in a reasoning chain |
   135→| `child_engrams` | IDs of engrams that follow from this one |
   136→| `related_engrams` | Typed relationships (follows_from, motivates, depends_on, supersedes, conflicts_with) |
   137→| `git_commits` | Code commits produced during this session |
   138→| `branch` | Git branch name |
   139→
   140→### Token Economics
   141→
   142→| Field | Description |
   143→|-------|-------------|
   144→| `input_tokens` | Tokens sent to the model |
   145→| `output_tokens` | Tokens received from the model |
   146→| `cache_read_tokens` | Tokens served from prompt cache |
   147→| `cache_write_tokens` | Tokens written to prompt cache |
   148→| `total_tokens` | Sum of all token fields |
   149→| `cost_usd` | Estimated cost in USD |
   150→
   151→---
   152→
   153→## Session Capture
   154→
   155→**Command:** `engram record -- <command> [args...]`
   156→
   157→Wraps any AI agent command in a PTY (pseudo-terminal) to capture its full session.
   158→
   159→**How it works:**
   160→
   161→1. Snapshots the working tree (SHA-256 hash of every tracked file, respecting `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, and global gitignore via the `ignore` crate)
   162→2. Creates an `ActiveSession` (`.git/engram-session` with `fs2` advisory file locking)
   163→3. Spawns the command in a PTY with separate reader/writer threads
   164→4. Captures all stdout/stderr output
   165→5. After exit, re-snapshots the working tree and diffs to detect file changes
   166→6. Runs heuristic dead-end/decision extraction on the raw output
   167→7. Builds and stores the engram, incrementally updates the search index
   168→
   169→**Dead-end / decision extraction heuristics** (case-insensitive patterns on raw output):
   170→
   171→| Pattern | Extracted as |
   172→|---------|-------------|
   173→| "tried X but Y" | Dead end |
   174→| "rejected X because Y" | Dead end |
   175→| "X didn't work because Y" | Dead end |
   176→| "instead of X" | Dead end |
   177→| "decided to X because Y" | Decision |
   178→| "chose X over Y" | Decision |
   179→
   180→**Options:**
   181→
   182→| Flag | Description |
   183→|------|-------------|
   184→| `--agent NAME` | Agent name (auto-detected from command if omitted) |
   185→| `--model MODEL` | Model name (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-4o`) |
   186→
   187→---
   188→
   189→## Session Import
   190→
   191→**Command:** `engram import [path] [--format FORMAT] [--auto-detect] [--dry-run]`
   192→
   193→Import reasoning sessions from existing AI coding tools.
   194→
   195→### Claude Code Import
   196→
   197→Parses Claude Code JSONL session files from `~/.claude/projects/`.
   198→
   199→**Capabilities:**
   200→- Auto-discovers session files by converting the repo path to Claude's project key format (e.g., `/Users/name/project` -> `-Users-name-project`)
   201→- Parses JSONL entries with flexible content blocks: text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking
   202→- Extracts model name from the first assistant message
   203→- Accumulates token usage including cache tokens (cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens)
   204→- Tracks file operations from Write/Edit/NotebookEdit tool calls
   205→- Captures agent version from session metadata
   206→- Skips sidechain messages
   207→
   208→### Aider Import
   209→
   210→Parses Aider's `.aider.chat.history.md` markdown format.
   211→
   212→**Capabilities:**
   213→- Discovers `.aider.chat.history.md` in the repository root
   214→- Splits multi-session files by `# aider chat started at` headers
   215→- Parses user messages (`#### ` prefix), assistant responses (unprefixed), and system output (`> ` prefix)
   216→- Extracts token counts from `> Tokens: 3.2k sent, 245 received. Cost: $0.01` lines
   217→- Supports k/K/m/M suffixes for token numbers (e.g., `3.2k` = 3200)
   218→- Each session in a file gets a unique source hash: `SHA256(file_hash:index)`
   219→
   220→### Deduplication
   221→
   222→Both importers compute a SHA-256 `source_hash` from the source file content. Before storing, `find_by_source_hash()` checks if the hash already exists. Re-importing the same file is always safe.
   223→
   224→---
   225→
   226→## Search and Indexing
   227→
   228→**Command:** `engram search <query> [-n LIMIT]`
   229→
   230→Full-text search powered by Tantivy, stored at `.git/engram-index/`.
   231→
   232→**Indexed fields:**
   233→
   234→| Field | Searchable | Stored | Type |
   235→|-------|-----------|--------|------|
   236→| `id` | exact | yes | STRING |
   237→| `intent_request` | full-text | yes | TEXT |
   238→| `intent_summary` | full-text | yes | TEXT |
   239→| `transcript_text` | full-text | no | TEXT |
   240→| `agent_name` | exact | yes | STRING |
   241→| `agent_model` | exact | yes | STRING |
   242→| `created_at` | range | yes | DATE |
   243→| `file_paths` | full-text | yes | TEXT |
   244→| `dead_ends` | full-text | yes | TEXT |
   245→| `cost_usd` | range | yes | F64 |
   246→| `total_tokens` | range | yes | U64 |
   247→| `manifest_json` | no | yes | stored-only |
   248→
   249→**Search behavior:**
   250→- Queries are parsed by Tantivy's QueryParser across 5 fields: intent_request, intent_summary, transcript_text, dead_ends, file_paths
   251→- Results ranked by relevance score
   252→- Specialized `search_by_file(path, limit)` for file-specific lookups
   253→
   254→**Index lifecycle:**
   255→- Lazy creation on first search (`ensure_index`)
   256→- Incremental updates when creating or importing engrams (`index_engram`)
   257→- Full rebuild on demand (`engram reindex`)
   258→- Automatic rebuild after `engram pull` fetches new refs
   259→- 50MB writer heap allocation
   260→
   261→---
   262→
   263→## File Tracing
   264→
   265→**Command:** `engram trace <file>`
   266→
   267→Shows the complete reasoning history for a specific file across all engrams.
   268→
   269→- Lists every engram that created, modified, or deleted the file
   270→- Results sorted chronologically (oldest first)
   271→- Displays: short ID, date, agent name, summary, and change type
   272→- Powered by `search_by_file()` under the hood (limit: 100 results)
   273→
   274→---
   275→
   276→## Engram Diff
   277→
   278→**Command:** `engram diff <id_a> <id_b>`
   279→
   280→Compares two engrams side-by-side.
   281→
   282→**Comparison output:**
   283→
   284→| Section | Description |
   285→|---------|-------------|
   286→| Common files | Files modified by both engrams |
   287→| Only in A | Files unique to the first engram |
   288→| Only in B | Files unique to the second engram |
   289→| Token delta | Difference in total tokens (B - A) |
   290→| Cost delta | Difference in USD cost (B - A) |
   291→
   292→---
   293→
   294→## Context Graph
   295→
   296→**Command:** `engram graph [node] [--depth N] [--dot]`
   297→
   298→Builds a semantic reasoning graph over the codebase.
   299→
   300→**Node types:**
   301→- Engram (box shape in DOT) -- labeled with summary or short ID
   302→- File (note shape) -- source files touched by engrams
   303→- Agent (diamond shape) -- AI agents that created engrams
   304→- Commit (ellipse shape) -- Git commits linked to engrams
   305→
   306→**Edge types:**
   307→- Engram --UsedAgent--> Agent
   308→- Engram --TouchedFile--> File
   309→- File --ModifiedBy--> Engram
   310→- Engram --ProducedBy--> Commit
   311→- Engram --FollowsFrom--> Parent Engram (lineage)
   312→
   313→**Features:**
   314→- Full graph construction from all engrams
   315→- Subgraph extraction via BFS around a center node (e.g., `file:src/auth.rs`)
   316→- Configurable traversal depth (default: 2)
   317→- Node deduplication via HashSet
   318→
   319→**Output formats:**
   320→- Text -- node and edge listing with counts
   321→- JSON -- full node/edge data
   322→- Graphviz DOT -- with shapes, edge labels, left-to-right layout (`rankdir=LR`)
   323→
   324→---
   325→
   326→## Branch Review
   327→
   328→**Command:** `engram review <base>..<head>`
   329→
   330→Intent-based code review: read the chain of reasoning instead of line-by-line diffs.
   331→
   332→**How it works:**
   333→1. Resolves base and head refs
   334→2. Walks the git log (revwalk from head, hiding base)
   335→3. For each commit, parses the message for `Engram-Id:` trailers
   336→4. Deduplicates engram IDs
   337→5. Reads full engram data and aggregates
   338→
   339→**Output:**
   340→- Total commits in range
   341→- Number of engrams found
   342→- Aggregate token usage and cost
   343→- All files changed across engrams
   344→- Per-engram: short ID, commit SHA, summary
   345→
   346→---
   347→
   348→## PR Summary Generation
   349→
   350→**Command:** `engram pr-summary <base>..<head> [--format json|markdown]`
   351→
   352→Auto-generates structured PR descriptions from the engram chain.
   353→
   354→**Markdown output includes:**
   355→- Summary section with per-engram summaries
   356→- Files changed across all engrams
   357→- Dead ends explored (rejected approaches and reasons)
   358→- Token economics (total tokens, total cost)
   359→- Commit list
   360→- Bot attribution footer
   361→
   362→---
   363→
   364→## Reasoning Blame
   365→
   366→**Command:** `engram blame <file> [-n LIMIT]`
   367→
   368→Shows reasoning blame for a file -- who changed it, when, and why.
   369→
   370→**Output per engram:**
   371→- Short ID and date
   372→- Change type (created / modified / deleted / touched)
   373→- Agent name
   374→- Summary
   375→- Intent (if different from summary)
   376→- Dead ends encountered
   377→
   378→---
   379→
   380→## Statistics
   381→
   382→**Command:** `engram stats`
   383→
   384→Aggregate statistics across all engrams.
   385→
   386→**Output:**
   387→- Total engram count
   388→- Total tokens consumed
   389→- Total cost (USD)
   390→- Date range (earliest to latest)
   391→- Breakdown by agent name
   392→- Breakdown by capture mode (wrapper / import / sdk)
   393→
   394→---
   395→
   396→## Garbage Collection
   397→
   398→**Command:** `engram gc --older-than <duration> [--dry-run] [-y]`
   399→
   400→Removes engrams older than a specified duration.
   401→
   402→**Duration units:**
   403→- `d` -- days (e.g., `30d`)
   404→- `w` -- weeks (e.g., `4w`)
   405→- `m` -- months (30 days, e.g., `6m`)
   406→- `y` -- years (365 days, e.g., `1y`)
   407→
   408→**Safety:**
   409→- `--dry-run` previews what would be deleted
   410→- Interactive confirmation prompt (skip with `-y`)
   411→- Lists each engram to be deleted before proceeding
   412→
   413→---
   414→
   415→## Remote Sync (Push / Pull / Fetch)
   416→
   417→Engram refs sync alongside code via standard Git refspecs.
   418→
   419→### Push
   420→
   421→**Command:** `engram push [remote] [--dry-run]`
   422→
   423→- Pushes `refs/engrams/*` to the remote
   424→- Auto-configures refspecs on the remote if missing
   425→- Push refspec: `refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*`
   426→
   427→### Pull
   428→
   429→**Command:** `engram pull [remote]`
   430→
   431→- Fetches engram refs from the remote
   432→- Automatically rebuilds the search index if new refs were fetched
   433→
   434→### Fetch
   435→
   436→**Command:** `engram fetch [remote] [--dry-run]`
   437→
   438→- Fetches engram refs without rebuilding the index
   439→- Fetch refspec: `+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*` (force flag)
   440→
   441→### Refspec Management
   442→
   443→- `ensure_refspecs(repo, remote)` -- idempotent, adds engram refspecs to a specific remote
   444→- `ensure_all_refspecs(repo)` -- configures all remotes in the repository
   445→- Additive only (never removes existing refspecs)
   446→- Configured automatically during `engram init`
   447→
   448→---
   449→
   450→## Git Hooks Integration
   451→
   452→Installed automatically by `engram init`. Existing hooks are preserved via `.pre-engram` backups and chained.
   453→
   454→### prepare-commit-msg
   455→
   456→During an active recording session, injects trailers into commit messages:
   457→
   458→```
   459→Engram-Id: <32-char-id>
   460→Engram-Agent: <agent-name>/<model>
   461→Engram-Tokens: <total-tokens>
   462→Engram-Cost: $<cost>
   463→```
   464→
   465→Idempotent: skips injection if `Engram-Id:` is already present.
   466→
   467→### post-commit
   468→
   469→Records the new commit SHA to the active session file (`.git/engram-session`).
   470→
   471→### Session Locking
   472→
   473→- Active sessions stored as JSON in `.git/engram-session`
   474→- `fs2` advisory file locking for concurrent commit safety
   475→- Exclusive locks for writes, shared locks for reads
   476→
   477→### Hook Safety
   478→
   479→- Hooks fail silently to never break the git workflow
   480→- Unknown hook names are ignored with a debug log
   481→- Installation backs up existing hooks; uninstallation restores originals
   482→
   483→---
   484→
   485→## MCP Server
   486→
   487→**Command:** `engram mcp`
   488→
   489→Starts a Model Context Protocol server on stdio transport, exposing engram data to AI agents (e.g., Claude Desktop, Claude Code).
   490→
   491→**Implementation:** `engram-mcp` crate using `rmcp` v0.15 with `schemars` v1 for JSON schema generation. Stores `PathBuf` instead of `git2::Repository` because `Repository` is `!Send` and rmcp requires `Send + Sync + 'static`. Each tool opens the repo fresh per request.
   492→
   493→### Tools
   494→
   495→| Tool | Parameters | Description |
   496→|------|-----------|-------------|
   497→| `engram_search` | `query`, `limit?` (default: 10) | Full-text search across intent, transcript, files, dead ends |
   498→| `engram_show` | `id` (or "HEAD") | Full engram details: manifest, intent, file changes, dead ends, decisions |
   499→| `engram_log` | `limit?` (default: 10), `by_agent?` | List recent engrams with tokens and cost |
   500→| `engram_trace` | `file_path` | Chronological reasoning history for a file |
   501→| `engram_diff` | `id_a`, `id_b` | Compare two engrams (files, tokens, cost) |
   502→| `engram_dead_ends` | `id?`, `query?` | Surface rejected approaches from one or all engrams |
   503→
   504→### Configuration (Claude Desktop)
   505→
   506→```json
   507→{
   508→  "mcpServers": {
   509→    "engram": {
   510→      "command": "engram",
   511→      "args": ["mcp"]
   512→    }
   513→  }
   514→}
   515→```
   516→
   517→---
   518→
   519→## SDK Integration
   520→
   521→Three SDKs with identical fluent APIs for programmatic engram creation.
   522→
   523→### Rust SDK
   524→
   525→**Crate:** `engram-sdk`
   526→
   527→```rust
   528→use engram_sdk::EngramSession;
   529→
   530→let mut session = EngramSession::begin("my-agent", Some("claude-sonnet-4-5"));
   531→```
   532→
   533→**Session lifecycle methods** (all return `&mut Self` for chaining):
   534→
   535→| Method | Description |
   536→|--------|-------------|
   537→| `log_message(role, content)` | Log conversation message (first user message auto-captured as original_request) |
   538→| `log_tool_call(name, input, output?)` | Log tool invocation (parses JSON input) |
   539→| `log_file_change(path, change_type)` | Track file modification (created/modified/deleted) |
   540→| `log_shell_command(cmd, exit_code?, duration?)` | Log shell command execution |
   541→| `log_rejection(approach, reason)` | Record rejected approach (dead end) |
   542→| `log_decision(description, rationale)` | Record architectural decision |
   543→| `add_tokens(input, output, cost?)` | Accumulate token usage (additive across calls) |
   544→| `set_summary(summary)` | Set session summary |
   545→| `tag(tag)` | Add a tag |
   546→| `parent(parent_id)` | Link to parent engram |
   547→| `agent_version(version)` | Set agent version |
   548→
   549→**Finalization:**
   550→
   551→| Method | Description |
   552→|--------|-------------|
   553→| `commit(git_sha?, summary?)` | Auto-discovers repo, stores engram, returns `EngramId` |
   554→| `commit_to(storage, git_sha?, summary?)` | Stores to a specific `GitStorage` instance |
   555→| `build(git_sha?, summary?)` | Builds `EngramData` without storing (for testing) |
   556→
   557→**Re-exports:** `AgentInfo`, `CaptureMode`, `EngramData`, `EngramId`, `FileChange`, `FileChangeType`, `GitStorage`, `Manifest`, `TokenUsage`
   558→
   559→### Python SDK
   560→
   561→**Package:** `engram` (Python >= 3.9, uses git CLI)
   562→
   563→```python
   564→from engram import EngramSession
   565→
   566→with EngramSession("my-agent", "claude-sonnet-4-5") as session:
   567→    session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication")
   568→    # Auto-commits on context manager exit
   569→```
   570→
   571→**API parity with Rust SDK**, plus:

content.text:
Now I have a thorough understanding of the project. Let me think about this strategically. Engram is a Git-native AI reasoning capture system. The core infrastructure is solid — storage, capture, import, query, sync, MCP server, three SDKs. Let me think about what would make this significantly more valuable.

Let me think about the different dimensions of value:

1. **Adoption / Distribution** — How do more people start using it?
2. **Data Value** — How do you make the captured data more useful?
3. **Integration Breadth** — Supporting more agents/tools
4. **Team/Enterprise Value** — Making it valuable for teams, not just individuals


5. **Developer Experience** — Making it easier and more seamless

The real bottleneck is adoption friction. Right now capture requires explicit commands or SDK calls, which creates friction. The biggest win would be eliminating that friction entirely — integrating with Claude Code through hooks so sessions auto-capture without any user action, or building a VS Code extension that captures seamlessly in the background.

Beyond capture, the second priority is turning raw data into insights. A richer analytics dashboard showing cost breakdowns by file and feature branch, pattern detection across sessions, and token optimization suggestions would unlock the real value of having all this data.

Then there's the enterprise angle: a shared engram server that aggregates across repos, GitHub Actions for automatic PR summaries, org-wide cost tracking and reasoning search, plus compliance features that create an auditable chain for every AI-generated change.

For integration breadth, I'm thinking about bringing in Cursor sessions alongside the existing tools. I'm organizing these feature ideas into a coherent roadmap that prioritizes what matters most for getting engrams into developers' hands quickly.

Here's where I'd focus, ordered by impact-to-effort ratio:

---

## 1. Zero-Friction Capture (highest leverage)

The biggest value blocker is adoption friction. The data model and query layer are strong — the gap is that users must remember to use `engram record` or call the SDK. Three moves here:

**Claude Code hooks integration** — Claude Code supports `hooks` in `.claude/settings.json` (pre/post tool calls, session start/stop). A single `engram init --claude-code` that installs a post-session hook to auto-capture would mean zero behavior change for the largest AI coding audience. Users install once and every session is captured automatically.

**GitHub Action for PR summaries** — `engram pr-summary` already works. A published GitHub Action (`uses: atticai/engram-action@v1`) that runs on every PR would give teams instant value. This is probably a weekend of work and it's also your best distribution channel — people discover it on the GitHub Marketplace.

**More importers** — Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, and Codex all have session data in various formats. Each new importer widens the addressable user base. Cursor alone is probably worth more adoption than the other three combined.

## 2. Making the Data Actionable (the "aha" moment)

Raw engram storage is infrastructure. The value inflection is when engram tells you something you didn't already know:

**Cost analytics** — `engram stats` is a start, but: cost per file, cost per feature branch, cost trend over the last 30 days, most expensive areas of code. This is the first thing engineering managers would pay for. The data is already there — it just needs aggregation and presentation.

**Recurring dead-end detection** — You already capture dead ends. Cross-session analysis that says "you've hit this same wall 3 times — here's what finally worked" is genuinely new capability that no other tool provides. This is engram's unique moat.

**`engram why <file>` or `engram why <file>:<line>`** — Go beyond `blame` (which shows *who* changed it) to show *why* it exists, by tracing through the reasoning chain. This is the killer demo — someone runs it on a confusing piece of code and gets the full reasoning history back.

## 3. Team / Enterprise Value (monetization path)

**Shared dashboard** — A lightweight web UI (even a static site generator, like `engram dashboard --serve`) that renders engrams as browsable HTML. Cost breakdowns by agent, by developer, by time period. This is the thing a team lead opens in a browser and immediately sees the value of.

**Audit trail** — "Every AI-generated change in our codebase has a traceable reasoning chain" is a compliance story that sells itself to enterprise. The `Engram-Id:` commit trailers already create the linkage — you just need to surface it in a way that satisfies audit requirements (exportable reports, tamper-evident via Git signatures).

**Cross-repo search** — Right now each repo has its own engram index. A central server (or even just a CLI that walks multiple repos) that answers "has anyone on the team solved this problem before?" across all projects.

## 4. Developer Experience Polish

**Interactive TUI** — `engram browse` with ratatui: scroll through engrams, expand/collapse sections, search inline. This turns engram from a CLI tool into an experience.

**VS Code / IDE extension** — Panel that shows the reasoning history for the file you're currently editing. When you open `auth.rs`, you see every engram that touched it, what was tried, what was decided.

---

## Where I'd actually start

If I had to pick **one thing** to build next, it would be the **GitHub Action for PR summaries**. Reasons:

1. It's small scope (the `pr-summary` command already exists)
2. It's the best distribution mechanism (people discover it on PRs, in the Marketplace)
3. It demonstrates the value proposition immediately — reviewers see *why* the code was written, not just *what* changed
4. It creates a natural pull toward the rest of the tool ("where did this summary come from? Oh, engram...")

Second would be the **Claude Code hooks auto-capture**, because it eliminates the adoption barrier for the most likely early users.

Design a detailed implementation plan for two features in the Engram project at /Users/sjonas/engram:

## Feature 1: GitHub Action for PR Summaries

**Context:** Engram already has `engram pr-summary base..head --format markdown` which generates markdown PR summaries from reasoning data stored in git refs. We need a GitHub Action that runs this on PRs automatically and posts the result as a sticky comment.

**Architecture decision:** Composite action in `action/` directory within the monorepo.

**What exists:**
- `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/pr_summary.rs` — generates markdown/json/text PR summaries
- `crates/engram-query/src/review.rs` — `review_branch()` walks commits for Engram-Id trailers
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — existing CI with fmt, clippy, test, build jobs

**What we need to build:**

1. **`action/action.yml`** — Composite action definition:
   - Inputs: `version` (default: latest), `github-token` (default: github.token), `format` (default: markdown)
   - Steps: checkout with full history, fetch engram refs, install engram binary from GitHub Release, run `engram pr-summary`, post as sticky PR comment using `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2`
   - Use `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` and `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` for the range
   - Branding: icon 'cpu', color 'purple'

2. **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — Release workflow triggered on `v*` tags:
   - Build matrix: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-apple-darwin
   - Use `cross` for Linux musl targets (static linking), native cargo for macOS
   - Upload tarballs named `engram-{target}.tar.gz` to GitHub Release via `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`
   - Consider: Linux musl needs `cross-rs` or `cargo-zigbuild`, macOS needs native runners

3. **`action/install.sh`** — Helper script for binary download:
   - Maps runner.os/arch to Rust target triples
   - Downloads from GitHub Release API
   - Extracts to a location on PATH

**Key considerations:**
- engram requires git2 which has vendored libgit2+openssl — musl static linking should work with vendored features
- The action needs `git fetch origin '+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*'` since actions/checkout doesn't fetch custom refs
- If no engrams exist yet, the action should post a helpful "no engrams found" message, not fail
- Need `engram init` to run before pr-summary if not already initialized

## Feature 2: Claude Code Auto-Capture via SessionEnd Hook

**Context:** Claude Code has a `SessionEnd` hook that fires when a conversation terminates. It provides `session_id` and `transcript_path` in the input JSON. This is perfect for auto-importing sessions.

**Architecture decision:** New `engram init --claude-code` CLI flag.

**What exists:**
- `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/init.rs` — InitArgs with `force` and `remote` flags
- `crates/engram-capture/src/import/claude_code.rs` — ClaudeCodeImporter with `import_session(path)` 
- `crates/engram-core/src/hooks/installer.rs` — hook installation system
- Existing auto-capture in hook_handler.rs that discovers Claude Code sessions on commit

**SessionEnd hook input JSON format:**
```json
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../session.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/sjonas/engram",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "SessionEnd",
  "reason": "prompt_input_exit"
}
```

**What we need to build:**

1. **Add `--claude-code` flag to `InitArgs`** in init.rs

2. **Claude Code hook installer** — new function that:
   - Reads or creates `.claude/settings.json` in the project root
   - Adds a `SessionEnd` hook entry that calls `engram import --session-file <path>`
   - The hook command should read stdin JSON to extract `transcript_path`, then call engram import on it
   - Must be idempotent (don't duplicate if already present)
   - The command could be a one-liner: `echo '$ARGUMENTS' | jq -r .transcript_path | xargs engram import --format claude-code`
   - Or better: a small shell script or `engram hook-handler session-end` subcommand that reads stdin

3. **New `engram import --session-file <path>`** or extend existing import to accept a direct path to a specific JSONL file (the current import does auto-discovery, but the hook provides the exact file)

4. **Update init.rs `run()` function** to call the Claude Code hook installer when `--claude-code` is set

**Key considerations:**
- The hook should use `"async": true` since we don't want to block session exit
- Need to handle the case where engram isn't on PATH (use absolute path or $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR)
- The `.claude/settings.json` might not exist yet — need to create it
- Must preserve any existing settings in the file
- The import already has deduplication via source_hash, so double-imports are safe
- The existing `engram import` command already accepts a path argument — check if it handles a single file directly

**Design the exact file changes needed, in order, with key code snippets. Consider error handling and edge cases.**

# Plan: GitHub Action + Claude Code Auto-Capture

## Context

Engram has a solid core (storage, capture, import, query, sync) but adoption requires two things: (1) zero-effort visibility into AI reasoning on PRs, and (2) zero-effort session capture. This plan adds both:

- **GitHub Action** that auto-posts `engram pr-summary` as a sticky PR comment
- **Claude Code SessionEnd hook** that auto-imports sessions when Claude Code exits

## Feature 1: GitHub Action for PR Summaries

### Files to Create

**`action/action.yml`** — Composite action (no Docker, no Node.js)
- Inputs: `version` (default: latest), `github-token` (default: `${{ github.token }}`)
- Steps:
  1. Fetch engram refs: `git fetch origin '+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*'`
  2. Install engram binary via `action/install.sh`
  3. Run `engram init` (idempotent, safe if already initialized)
  4. Run `engram pr-summary $BASE..$HEAD --format markdown`, capture output
  5. Post as sticky PR comment via `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2` with header `engram-pr-summary`
  6. If no engrams found, post a helpful onboarding message instead
- Branding: icon `cpu`, color `purple`
- Note: the calling workflow is responsible for `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0`

**`action/install.sh`** — Binary download helper
- Maps `RUNNER_OS`/`RUNNER_ARCH` to Rust target triples (linux-musl, darwin)
- Downloads tarball from GitHub Releases API (`latest` or pinned version)
- Installs to `$HOME/.engram/bin`, adds to `$GITHUB_PATH`

**`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — Cross-platform release builds on `v*` tags
- Build matrix: 4 targets
  - `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (ubuntu-latest, `cross`)
  - `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` (ubuntu-latest, `cross`)
  - `x86_64-apple-darwin` (macos-13)
  - `aarch64-apple-darwin` (macos-14)
- Linux uses `cross-rs/cross` for musl static linking (vendored deps make this work)
- macOS uses native cargo on arch-appropriate runners
- Packages as `engram-{target}.tar.gz`, uploads via `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`

### Consumer Usage

```yaml
name: Engram PR Summary
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
permissions:
  pull-requests: write
  contents: read
jobs:
  engram:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK@v1
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

---

## Feature 2: Claude Code Auto-Capture

Claude Code's `SessionEnd` hook fires when a conversation terminates, providing `transcript_path` on stdin as JSON. This is the exact file path `ClaudeCodeImporter::import_session()` needs.

### Files to Create

**`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/claude_code.rs`** — Hook installer/uninstaller
- `install_claude_code_hook(project_root: &Path) -> Result<(), CoreError>`
  - Creates `.claude/settings.json` if needed (preserves existing content)
  - Adds `SessionEnd` hook entry that calls `engram hook-handler session-end`
  - Uses `std::env::current_exe()` for absolute path to engram binary
  - Idempotent: checks for existing `engram hook-handler session-end` marker
- `uninstall_claude_code_hook(project_root: &Path) -> Result<(), CoreError>`
  - Removes the engram hook entry, preserves everything else

### Files to Modify

**`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/mod.rs`** — Add `pub mod claude_code;` and re-export

**`crates/engram-cli/src/commands/init.rs`** — Add `--claude-code` flag to `InitArgs`
- When set, call `hooks::install_claude_code_hook(workdir)`
- Works even when already initialized (no `--force` needed just to add the hook)
- Print confirmation: "Claude Code SessionEnd hook configured."

**`crates/engram-cli/src/commands/hook_handler.rs`** — Add `session-end` match arm
- New function `handle_session_end(storage: &GitStorage)`:
  1. Read JSON from stdin, extract `transcript_path`
  2. Verify file exists
  3. Call `ClaudeCodeImporter::import_session(path)`
  4. Check for duplicate via `find_by_source_hash()`
  5. Store engram, best-effort index update
  6. All errors logged at debug level, never propagated (silent failure)
- Follows exact pattern of existing `maybe_auto_capture()` at lines 60-162

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionEnd": [
      {
        "matcher": "",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "/absolute/path/to/engram hook-handler session-end"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

---

## Implementation Order

1. `crates/engram-core/src/hooks/claude_code.rs` — new file, hook installer with tests
2. `crates/engram-core/src/hooks/mod.rs` — add module + re-exports
3. `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/hook_handler.rs` — add `session-end` handler
4. `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/init.rs` — add `--claude-code` flag
5. `action/action.yml` — composite action definition
6. `action/install.sh` — binary installer script
7. `.github/workflows/release.yml` — cross-platform release workflow

## Verification

1. **Rust compilation:** `source "$HOME/.cargo/env" && cargo build --workspace`
2. **Tests:** `cargo test --workspace` (all 118 existing + new claude_code tests)
3. **Clippy:** `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
4. **Format:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
5. **Manual test of `--claude-code`:** Run `cargo run -p engram-cli -- init --claude-code --force` in a test repo, verify `.claude/settings.json` has the correct hook
6. **Idempotency:** Run `init --claude-code` twice, verify no duplicate hook entries

name: 'Engram PR Summary'
description: 'Post AI reasoning summaries on pull requests using Engram'
author: 'AtticAI Inc.'
branding:
  icon: 'cpu'
  color: 'purple'

inputs:
  version:
    description: 'Engram CLI version to install (e.g., "v0.1.0" or "latest")'
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  github-token:
    description: 'GitHub token for posting PR comments'
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.token }}

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Fetch engram refs
      shell: bash
      run: git fetch origin '+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*' 2>/dev/null || true

    - name: Install engram
      shell: bash
      run: bash "${{ github.action_path }}/install.sh"
      env:
        ENGRAM_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github-token }}

    - name: Initialize engram
      shell: bash
      run: engram init 2>/dev/null || true

    - name: Generate PR summary
      id: summary
      shell: bash
      run: |
        BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
        HEAD="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
        RANGE="${BASE}..${HEAD}"

        OUTPUT=$(engram pr-summary "$RANGE" --format markdown 2>&1) || true

        if [ -z "$OUTPUT" ] || echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -qi "no engrams found"; then
          echo "has_summary=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        else
          # Write multiline output using a random delimiter
          EOF=$(dd if=/dev/urandom bs=15 count=1 status=none | base64)
          {
            echo "has_summary=true"
            echo "body<<$EOF"
            echo "$OUTPUT"
            echo "$EOF"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        fi

    - name: Post PR summary comment
      if: steps.summary.outputs.has_summary == 'true'
      uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2
      with:
        header: engram-pr-summary
        message: ${{ steps.summary.outputs.body }}
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github-token }}

    - name: Post no-data comment
      if: steps.summary.outputs.has_summary == 'false'
      uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2
      with:
        header: engram-pr-summary
        message: |
          **Engram:** No reasoning data found for this PR.

          To capture AI reasoning, use one of:
          - `engram init --claude-code` for automatic Claude Code session capture
          - `engram record -- <agent-command>` to record agent sessions
          - `engram import --auto-detect` to import existing sessions

          [Learn more](https://github.com/AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK)
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github-token }}

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Install the engram CLI binary from GitHub Releases.
# Expected environment variables:
#   ENGRAM_VERSION  - Tag to install (e.g. "v0.1.0" or "latest")
#   RUNNER_OS       - GitHub Actions runner OS (Linux, macOS)
#   RUNNER_ARCH     - GitHub Actions runner arch (X64, ARM64)
#   GITHUB_PATH     - GitHub Actions path file (for adding to PATH)

REPO="AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK"
VERSION="${ENGRAM_VERSION:-latest}"
OS="${RUNNER_OS:-Linux}"
ARCH="${RUNNER_ARCH:-X64}"

# Map GitHub Actions runner environment to Rust target triples
case "${OS}-${ARCH}" in
  Linux-X64)    TARGET="x86_64-unknown-linux-musl" ;;
  Linux-ARM64)  TARGET="aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" ;;
  macOS-X64)    TARGET="x86_64-apple-darwin" ;;
  macOS-ARM64)  TARGET="aarch64-apple-darwin" ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::Unsupported platform: ${OS}-${ARCH}"
    exit 1
    ;;

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            use_cross: true
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            use_cross: true
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-13
            use_cross: false
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-14
            use_cross: false

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install cross
        if: matrix.use_cross
        run: cargo install cross --git https://github.com/cross-rs/cross

      - name: Build (cross)
        if: matrix.use_cross
        run: cross build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p engram-cli

      - name: Build (cargo)
        if: ${{ !matrix.use_cross }}
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p engram-cli

      - name: Package
        run: |
          cd target/${{ matrix.target }}/release
          tar czf ../../../engram-${{ matrix.target }}.tar.gz engram

      - name: Upload release assets
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: engram-${{ matrix.target }}.tar.gz

Here's a summary of everything that was built:

## Feature 1: GitHub Action for PR Summaries

**3 new files:**

- **`action/action.yml`** — Composite GitHub Action. Users add it to their PR workflow and get automatic sticky comments with AI reasoning summaries (which engrams contributed, files changed, dead ends, token costs). Falls back to a helpful onboarding message if no engrams exist yet.

- **`action/install.sh`** — Downloads the correct platform binary (linux-musl or macOS, x64 or arm64) from GitHub Releases. Maps `RUNNER_OS`/`RUNNER_ARCH` to Rust target triples.

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — Cross-platform release workflow triggered on `v*` tags. Builds static binaries for 4 targets using `cross` for Linux musl and native cargo for macOS. Uploads tarballs to the GitHub Release.

**Consumer usage:**
```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- uses: AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK@v1
```

## Feature 2: Claude Code Auto-Capture

**1 new file, 3 modified:**

- **`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/claude_code.rs`** (new) — `install_claude_code_hook()` and `uninstall_claude_code_hook()`. Reads/creates `.claude/settings.json`, adds a `SessionEnd` hook that calls `engram hook-handler session-end`. Idempotent, preserves existing settings. 6 unit tests.

- **`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/mod.rs`** — Added module + re-exports.

- **`crates/engram-cli/src/commands/hook_handler.rs`** — Added `handle_session_end()` function and `"session-end"` match arm. Reads Claude Code's JSON from stdin, extracts `transcript_path`, imports via `ClaudeCodeImporter`, stores with dedup check. All errors silently logged.

- **`crates/engram-cli/src/commands/init.rs`** — Added `--claude-code` flag. Works on both fresh init and already-initialized repos.

**User experience:**
```bash
engram init --claude-code
# "Claude Code SessionEnd hook configured.
#   Sessions will be auto-imported when Claude Code exits."
```

After that, every Claude Code session in the repo is automatically captured as an engram when the conversation ends — zero ongoing effort.

Engram makes reasoning first-class, versioned, and queryable, stored in Git itself.
     6→

   288→| `push`        | Push engram refs to a remote |
   289→| `pull`        | Pull engram refs and reindex |
   290→| `fetch`       | Fetch engram refs from a remote |

input.new_string:
## Claude Code Auto-Capture

Automatically capture every Claude Code session as an engram -- zero ongoing effort:

```bash
engram init --claude-code
```

This installs a `SessionEnd` hook in `.claude/settings.json` that fires when Claude Code exits. The hook reads the session transcript and imports it as an engram with full deduplication. Works on both fresh repos and repos already initialized with engram.

## GitHub Action

Post AI reasoning summaries on every pull request:

```yaml
name: Engram PR Summary
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
permissions:
  pull-requests: write
  contents: read
jobs:
  engram:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK@v1
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

The action fetches engram refs, runs `engram pr-summary`, and posts a sticky comment with the reasoning chain, files changed, dead ends explored, and token economics. If no engrams are found, it posts a helpful onboarding message instead.

## Git Hooks Integration

When you run `engram init`, git hooks are automatically installed:

- **prepare-commit-msg**: Injects `Engram-Id:` and `Engram-Agent:` trailers into commit messages during active recording sessions
- **post-commit**: Links new commit SHAs to the active session for automatic commit tracking

Existing hooks are preserved -- engram chains after them via `.pre-engram` backups. Hooks fail silently to never break your git workflow.

## Context: Existing Primitives

**Data available per engram (from Manifest/EngramData):**
- `token_usage`: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd
- `agent`: name, model, version
- `created_at`, `finished_at`
- `git_commits`: linked commit SHAs
- `operations.file_changes`: Vec<FileChange> with path, change_type (Created/Modified/Deleted/Renamed), lines_added, lines_removed
- `intent.dead_ends`: Vec<DeadEnd> with approach, reason
- `intent.decisions`: Vec<Decision> with description, rationale
- `intent.original_request`, `intent.interpreted_goal`, `intent.summary`
- `lineage.branch`: Optional branch name

**Existing query capabilities:**
- `GitStorage::list(opts)` — enumerate all engrams with optional agent filter and limit, sorted by created_at desc
- `GitStorage::read(id)` — load full EngramData
- `GitStorage::read_manifest(id)` — fast path, manifest only
- `SearchEngine::search_by_file(path, limit)` — find engrams touching a file
- `trace_file(storage, search, path)` — chronological file history

**Existing CLI patterns:**
- Commands in `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/` as separate files
- Registered in `mod.rs` Commands enum with clap Args structs  
- Dispatched in `main.rs` match block
- All support `OutputFormat` (Text, Json, Markdown) via `--format` flag
- Stats command at `stats.rs` already aggregates totals, by-agent, by-capture-mode

**Key file paths:**
- `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/stats.rs` — current stats (totals + by-agent + by-mode + date range)
- `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/blame.rs` — file blame (lists engrams per file with change type)
- `crates/engram-cli/src/commands/trace.rs` — file trace (chronological)
- `crates/engram-query/src/search.rs` — SearchEngine
- `crates/engram-query/src/trace.rs` — trace_file()
- `crates/engram-core/src/model/intent.rs` — DeadEnd { approach, reason }, Decision { description, rationale }
- `crates/engram-core/src/model/operations.rs` — FileChange, lines_added/removed
- `crates/engram-core/src/model/token_economics.rs` — TokenUsage with cost_usd
- `crates/engram-mcp/src/lib.rs` — 6 MCP tools

---

## Feature 1: Enhanced Cost Analytics (`engram stats` improvements)

Enhance the existing `engram stats` command with:

### 1a. Cost per file (`engram stats --by-file`)
For each file touched across all engrams, show how many times it was modified and the proportional cost. A file's cost share = (engram_cost / num_files_in_that_engram) summed across all engrams that touch it.

### 1b. Cost per branch (`engram stats --by-branch`)  
Group engrams by `lineage.branch` and show per-branch totals.

### 1c. Cost trend (`engram stats --trend`)
Show cost and token usage bucketed by day/week over the last 30 days.

### 1d. Most expensive engrams (`engram stats --top N`)
Show the N most expensive engrams by cost.

Design approach: Extend the existing `stats.rs` with new subflags. All data needed is already in Manifest (fast path via read_manifest) and full EngramData (for file changes). The `list()` function provides the iteration.

---

## Feature 2: `engram why <file>` — Rich Reasoning Narrative

A new CLI command that answers "why does this file exist / why was it changed?" by showing the full reasoning chain.

**Output style**: Rich narrative — for each engram that touched the file (chronological):
- Date and agent/model
- Original request that led to the change
- What was decided and why
- Dead ends explored related to the file
- How the file was changed (created/modified/deleted)
- Interpreted goal

This is distinct from `blame` (which is compact, one-line-per-engram) and `trace` (which just shows IDs/summaries). `why` tells the full story.

**Implementation**: New command file `why.rs`. Uses `search_by_file()` to find engrams, then reads full data for each. Also consider adding this as a new MCP tool `engram_why` so AI agents can query reasoning.

---

## Feature 3: Recurring Dead-End Detection (`engram dead-ends --recurring`)

Cross-session analysis that finds dead ends appearing in multiple engrams.

**Algorithm**:
1. Iterate all engrams, collect all dead ends with their engram IDs
2. Normalize dead-end approaches (lowercase, trim)
3. Group by similar approach text (exact match first, could add fuzzy later)
4. Filter to groups with count >= 2
5. For each recurring dead end, show: approach, reason, count, which engrams hit it

This could be:
- A flag on the existing `dead-ends` MCP tool
- A new CLI subcommand
- Both

Also add an MCP tool variant so AI agents can check "am I about to repeat a known dead end?"

---

## Design Requirements

For each feature:
1. List exact files to create/modify with key code structure
2. Follow existing patterns (clap Args, OutputFormat, error handling)
3. Add library functions in engram-query where appropriate (not just CLI)
4. Add corresponding MCP tools where useful for AI agents
5. Include tests
6. Consider what new data structures are needed (put in engram-query, not CLI)

Prioritize: Keep it simple. Use existing list/read patterns. Don't add new dependencies unless absolutely necessary. Don't over-abstract — these are query/aggregation features, not new storage mechanisms.

All 5 tasks complete. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

## Summary

### 3 New Features Implemented

**1. Enhanced `engram stats`** — Added `StatsArgs` with 4 new flags:
- `--by-file`: Cost/token breakdown per file touched (distributes session cost across files)
- `--by-branch`: Cost/token breakdown per branch
- `--trend`: Daily cost trend for the last 30 days
- `--top N`: Limits breakdown entries (default: 10)

**2. `engram why <file>`** — Rich narrative explaining why a file exists:
- Traces the full reasoning chain chronologically
- Shows for each session: request, goal, result, change type, dead ends, decisions
- Footer with aggregate stats (sessions, tokens, cost)
- JSON output support

**3. `engram dead-ends`** — New CLI command for dead-end analysis:
- `--recurring`: Cross-session detection of approaches tried and rejected multiple times
- `--query`: Text filter across approach/reason
- `--id`: Dead ends from a specific engram
- `--top N`: Limit results

### MCP Tools Added
- `engram_stats`: Aggregate stats with `by_file`, `by_branch`, `trend` params
- `engram_why`: Explain a file's reasoning history
- `engram_dead_ends` updated: Added `recurring` parameter

1→# Engram
     2→
     3→**Capture agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git.**
     4→
     5→Git commits capture *what* changed but discard *why*. When AI agents code, the reasoning trail -- 100K+ tokens of explored alternatives, architectural tradeoffs, rejected approaches -- IS the institutional knowledge. Engram makes reasoning first-class, versioned, and queryable, stored in Git itself.
     6→
     7→Each **engram** is a discrete unit of reasoning memory: the full session transcript, human intent, agent decisions, tool calls, dead ends explored, and token economics -- linked to the Git commits it produced.
     8→
     9→For Full Documentation and Guides, Visit: https://the-attic-ai.gitbook.io/untitled/
    10→
    11→## Quick Start
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→# Install from source
    15→git clone https://github.com/AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK.git
    16→cd Engram-SDK
    17→cargo install --path crates/engram-cli
    18→
    19→# Initialize in your repo (with automatic Claude Code capture)
    20→engram init --claude-code
    21→
    22→# Record an agent session (wraps any agent command in a PTY)
    23→engram record -- claude "add OAuth2 authentication"
    24→
    25→# Import existing sessions from Claude Code or Aider
    26→engram import --auto-detect
    27→
    28→# Explore reasoning history
    29→engram log --cost
    30→engram show HEAD --intent
    31→engram search "authentication"
    32→engram trace src/auth.rs
    33→
    34→# Review by intent, not by diff
    35→engram review main..feature-branch
    36→
    37→# Push reasoning alongside code
    38→engram push
    39→```
    40→
    41→## Why Engram?
    42→
    43→**Without Engram**, your Git history looks like:
    44→```
    45→abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow
    46→def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
    47→789abc Refactor auth to use sessions
    48→```
    49→
    50→**With Engram**, every commit carries its reasoning:
    51→```
    52→abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow [claude-code/claude-sonnet-4-5] $0.23 47832tok
    53→  Intent: "Add OAuth2 authentication with PKCE for our SPA"
    54→  Summary: Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE using custom middleware. Added
    55→           token refresh, CSRF protection, and session management.
    56→  Dead ends: Tried passport.js (middleware conflict), considered Auth0
    57→             SDK (added 2MB to bundle, decided against).
    58→  Files: +src/auth.rs +src/middleware/oauth.rs ~src/routes/api.rs
    59→
    60→def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
    61→  Intent: "The auth middleware runs after the rate limiter, causing 401s"
    62→  Summary: Reordered middleware stack. Auth must run before rate limiting.
    63→  Related: Follows from abc123 (the original auth implementation)
    64→```
    65→
    66→This is **institutional knowledge** that compounds. When the next agent (or human) touches auth, they see the full reasoning chain -- what was tried, what was rejected, and why.
    67→
    68→## Three Capture Modes
    69→
    70→### Mode 1: Wrapper (any agent)
    71→```bash
    72→engram record -- claude "add auth"
    73→engram record -- aider --model gpt-4o
    74→engram record -- cursor-cli "fix the bug"
    75→```
    76→Spawns your agent in a PTY, captures output, detects file changes via SHA256 snapshots. File change detection respects `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`, and global gitignore rules.
    77→
    78→### Mode 2: Session Import
    79→```bash
    80→engram import --auto-detect                              # Find and import from known agents
    81→engram import ~/.claude/projects/.../session.jsonl --format claude-code
    82→engram import .aider.chat.history.md --format aider
    83→engram import --dry-run                                  # Preview what would be imported
    84→```
    85→Parses Claude Code JSONL sessions and Aider chat history markdown. Extracts transcripts, tool calls, token usage, and file changes. Re-importing the same file is safe -- duplicate detection via content hashing prevents double imports.
    86→
    87→### Mode 3: SDK Integration
    88→
    89→**Rust:**
    90→```rust
    91→use engram_sdk::EngramSession;
    92→
    93→let mut session = EngramSession::begin("my-agent", Some("claude-sonnet-4-5"));
    94→session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication");
    95→session.log_message("assistant", "Implementing OAuth2 with PKCE...");
    96→session.log_tool_call("write_file", r#"{"path":"src/auth.rs"}"#, Some("Created auth module"));
    97→session.log_file_change("src/auth.rs", "created");
    98→session.log_rejection("passport.js", "Middleware conflict with existing stack");
    99→session.add_tokens(1500, 800, Some(0.02));
   100→let id = session.commit(Some("abc123"), Some("Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE")).unwrap();
   101→```
   102→
   103→**Python:**
   104→```python
   105→from engram import EngramSession
   106→
   107→with EngramSession("my-agent", "claude-sonnet-4-5") as session:
   108→    session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication")
   109→    session.log_message("assistant", "Implementing OAuth2 with PKCE...")
   110→    session.log_tool_call("write_file", {"path": "src/auth.rs"})
   111→    session.log_file_change("src/auth.rs", "created")
   112→    session.log_rejection("passport.js", "Middleware conflict")
   113→    session.add_tokens(1500, 800, 0.02)
   114→```
   115→
   116→**TypeScript:**
   117→```typescript
   118→import { EngramSession } from '@engram/sdk';
   119→
   120→const session = EngramSession.begin('my-agent', 'claude-sonnet-4-5');
   121→session.logMessage('user', 'Add OAuth2 authentication');
   122→session.logToolCall('write_file', { path: 'src/auth.rs' });
   123→session.logFileChange('src/auth.rs', 'created');
   124→session.logRejection('passport.js', 'Middleware conflict');
   125→session.addTokens(1500, 800, 0.02);
   126→const id = session.commit('abc123', 'Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE');
   127→```
   128→
   129→## Git-Native Storage
   130→
   131→Engrams are stored as native Git objects -- they travel with `clone`, `push`, `pull`. No sidecar database, no separate sync, no vendor lock-in.
   132→
   133→```
   134→.git/refs/engrams/
   135→  ab/
   136→    abc123...  -> commit -> tree containing:
   137→      manifest.json        # Compact metadata for fast listing
   138→      intent.md            # Human-readable reasoning summary
   139→      transcript.jsonl     # Full session, one message per line
   140→      operations.json      # Tool calls, file ops, shell commands
   141→      lineage.json         # Relationships to other engrams
   142→```
   143→
   144→Engrams sync alongside code:
   145→```bash
   146→engram push              # Push engram refs to remote
   147→engram pull              # Fetch engram refs and reindex
   148→engram fetch             # Fetch only (no reindex)
   149→```
   150→
   151→## Claude Code Auto-Capture
   152→
   153→Automatically capture every Claude Code session as an engram -- zero ongoing effort:
   154→
   155→```bash
   156→engram init --claude-code
   157→```
   158→
   159→This installs a `SessionEnd` hook in `.claude/settings.json` that fires when Claude Code exits. The hook reads the session transcript and imports it as an engram with full deduplication. Works on both fresh repos and repos already initialized with engram.
   160→
   161→## GitHub Action
   162→
   163→Post AI reasoning summaries on every pull request:
   164→
   165→```yaml
   166→name: Engram PR Summary
   167→on:
   168→  pull_request:
   169→    types: [opened, synchronize]
   170→permissions:
   171→  pull-requests: write
   172→  contents: read
   173→jobs:
   174→  engram:
   175→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   176→    steps:
   177→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   178→        with:
   179→          fetch-depth: 0
   180→      - uses: AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK@v1
   181→        with:
   182→          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   183→```
   184→
   185→The action fetches engram refs, runs `engram pr-summary`, and posts a sticky comment with the reasoning chain, files changed, dead ends explored, and token economics. If no engrams are found, it posts a helpful onboarding message instead.
   186→
   187→## Git Hooks Integration
   188→
   189→When you run `engram init`, git hooks are automatically installed:
   190→
   191→- **prepare-commit-msg**: Injects `Engram-Id:` and `Engram-Agent:` trailers into commit messages during active recording sessions
   192→- **post-commit**: Links new commit SHAs to the active session for automatic commit tracking
   193→
   194→Existing hooks are preserved -- engram chains after them via `.pre-engram` backups. Hooks fail silently to never break your git workflow.
   195→
   196→## Search and Query
   197→
   198→Full-text search powered by Tantivy, stored at `.git/engram-index/`:
   199→
   200→```bash
   201→# Search across intent, transcript, file paths, dead ends
   202→engram search "authentication"
   203→engram search "database migration" -n 20
   204→
   205→# Trace the full reasoning history of a file
   206→engram trace src/auth.rs
   207→
   208→# Compare two engrams (files, tokens, cost)
   209→engram diff abc123 def456
   210→
   211→# Rebuild search index from scratch
   212→engram reindex
   213→```
   214→
   215→The search index is automatically updated when creating or importing engrams.
   216→
   217→## Context Graph
   218→
   219→Engrams form a **context graph** -- a semantic reasoning layer over your codebase:
   220→
   221→```bash
   222→# Explore connections between engrams, files, and agents
   223→engram graph
   224→engram graph file:src/auth.rs --depth 2
   225→
   226→# Export as Graphviz DOT format
   227→engram graph --dot | dot -Tsvg -o graph.svg
   228→```
   229→
   230→Nodes are engrams, files, agents, and commits. Edges are "modified by", "used agent", "follows from", "touched file", "produced by".
   231→
   232→## Intent-Based Review
   233→
   234→```bash
   235→engram review main..feature-branch
   236→```
   237→
   238→Instead of line-by-line code review, read the chain of intents and summaries. See what was asked, what was done, what dead ends were explored, and what architectural decisions were made. Includes aggregate token usage and cost.
   239→
   240→## PR Summary
   241→
   242→Auto-generate structured PR descriptions from the engram chain:
   243→
   244→```bash
   245→engram pr-summary main..feature-branch
   246→engram pr-summary main..feature-branch --format json
   247→```
   248→
   249→Outputs a markdown PR description with summary, file changes, reasoning chain, dead ends, and token economics.
   250→
   251→## MCP Server
   252→
   253→Expose engram data to AI agents via the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io):
   254→
   255→```bash
   256→engram mcp
   257→```
   258→
   259→Starts an MCP server on stdio with 6 tools:
   260→
   261→| Tool | Parameters | Description |
   262→|------|-----------|-------------|
   263→| `engram_search` | `query`, `limit?` | Full-text search across intent, transcript, file paths, and dead ends |
   264→| `engram_show` | `id` (or `"HEAD"`) | Show full engram details: manifest, intent, file changes, decisions |
   265→| `engram_log` | `limit?`, `by_agent?` | List recent engrams with token usage and cost |
   266→| `engram_trace` | `file_path` | Chronological reasoning history for a specific file |
   267→| `engram_diff` | `id_a`, `id_b` | Compare two engrams: common/unique files, token and cost deltas |
   268→| `engram_dead_ends` | `id?`, `query?` | Surface rejected approaches and architectural decisions |
   269→
   270→### Claude Code
   271→
   272→Repos that include a `.mcp.json` file (like this one) are auto-configured — Claude Code will discover and start the engram MCP server automatically. No manual setup needed.
   273→
   274→To add engram MCP to any repo, create `.mcp.json` at the repo root:
   275→
   276→```json
   277→{
   278→  "mcpServers": {
   279→    "engram": {
   280→      "command": "engram",
   281→      "args": ["mcp"],
   282→      "env": {
   283→        "PATH": "${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"
   284→      }
   285→    }
   286→  }
   287→}
   288→```
   289→
   290→For global access across all projects, add the same config to `~/.claude/mcp.json`.
   291→
   292→### Claude Desktop
   293→
   294→Add to `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`):
   295→
   296→```json
   297→{
   298→  "mcpServers": {
   299→    "engram": {
   300→      "command": "engram",
   301→      "args": ["mcp"]
   302→    }
   303→  }
   304→}
   305→```
   306→
   307→## CLI Reference
   308→
   309→| Command       | Description |
   310→|---------------|-------------|
   311→| `init`        | Initialize engram in a Git repository (`--remote`, `--force`, `--claude-code`) |
   312→| `record`      | Record an agent session via PTY wrapper (`--agent`, `--model`) |
   313→| `import`      | Import sessions from Claude Code or Aider (with dedup) |
   314→| `log`         | List engrams (most recent first) (`--cost`, `--by-agent`) |
   315→| `show`        | Show details of a specific engram (supports `HEAD`) |
   316→| `search`      | Full-text search across engrams |
   317→| `trace`       | Show reasoning history for a file |
   318→| `diff`        | Compare two engrams |
   319→| `graph`       | Show the context graph (text or DOT) |
   320→| `review`      | Review intent chain for a branch range |
   321→| `pr-summary`  | Generate a PR description from the engram chain |
   322→| `mcp`         | Start MCP server (stdio) for AI agent integration |
   323→| `stats`       | Show aggregate statistics across all engrams |
   324→| `blame`       | Show reasoning blame for a file |
   325→| `gc`          | Garbage collect old engrams (`--older-than`, `--dry-run`) |
   326→| `push`        | Push engram refs to a remote |
   327→| `pull`        | Pull engram refs and reindex |
   328→| `fetch`       | Fetch engram refs from a remote |
   329→| `reindex`     | Rebuild the search index |
   330→| `version`     | Print version information |
   331→
   332→All commands support `--format json` for machine-readable output and `-v`/`-vv`/`-vvv` for verbosity.
   333→
   334→## Architecture
   335→
   336→```
   337→crates/
   338→  engram-core/       Data model, Git storage engine, hooks, config
   339→  engram-capture/    PTY wrapper, file change detection, session importers
   340→  engram-query/      Tantivy search index, context graph, branch review
   341→  engram-protocol/   Push/pull/fetch via Git refspecs
   342→  engram-sdk/        Fluent Rust SDK for direct agent integration
   343→  engram-mcp/        MCP server for AI agent integration (rmcp)
   344→  engram-cli/        CLI binary (installed as `engram`)
   345→sdks/
   346→  python/            Python SDK (git CLI)
   347→  typescript/        TypeScript SDK (git CLI)
   348→```
   349→
   350→### Design Principles
   351→
   352→- **Git-native**: Engrams are Git objects (blobs, trees, commits, refs). No external database.
   353→- **Zero config remotes**: Engram refs sync with standard `git push`/`fetch` via refspecs.
   354→- **Vendored dependencies**: git2 with vendored libgit2 + OpenSSL. No system deps beyond a C compiler.
   355→- **No unsafe code**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide.
   356→- **Library-first**: All functionality lives in library crates; the CLI is a thin wrapper.
   357→- **Cross-platform**: File locking via `fs2`, Unix-specific code guarded by `#[cfg(unix)]`.
   358→- **Safe imports**: Duplicate detection via SHA-256 content hashing prevents re-importing the same session.
   359→
   360→## Building from Source
   361→
   362→```bash
   363→# Clone and build
   364→git clone https://github.com/AtticAIInc/Engram-SDK.git
   365→cd Engram-SDK
   366→cargo build --workspace
   367→
   368→# Run tests (124 Rust + 10 Python + 7 TypeScript = 141 total)
   369→cargo test --workspace
   370→cd sdks/python && python3 -m pytest tests/
   371→cd sdks/typescript && npx vitest run
   372→
   373→# Lint
   374→cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
   375→
   376→# Install the CLI
   377→cargo install --path crates/engram-cli
   378→```
   379→
   380→Requires Rust 1.80+ and a C compiler (for vendored libgit2/OpenSSL).
